Definition: from G4862 and G726; to snatch together, i.e. seize:--catch.
BiblicalUsage: The unclean spirit had often caught the man and driven him into the wilderness, and on the voyage to Rome the ship was caught by the wind and could not bear up, so they let her drive. The same word seizes a man and a ship, and in both cases the thing seized is carried where it does not want to go.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that evil seizes and drives, and I hold that only Christ can break the grip of what has caught me.
